2106611316580667408.content_en: Seeing the much-talked-about 'FX Warrior Kurumi-chan', there may be many girls who try 'I'll aim for 20 million yen from 300,000 yen too!' and ruin themselves. I support them 🔥 But there were no prop firms in Kurumi-chan's era; if you're taking revenge for your mother now, prop is more advantageous and easier. Many people still find prop troublesome and don't understand it well, so let me explain the difference between FX and prop a bit more simply. For example: if you put 300,000 yen of cash saved from a part-time job into an account at overseas high-leverage Exness, the rules are free, leverage is unlimited, you can do anything, and all profits can be withdrawn, but you can only use 300,000 yen. Another example: if you buy a 20-million-yen demo account (instant, going straight to a live phase) at prop firm FundedElite for 300,000 yen, you're bound by detailed rules such as leverage, but you can trade a 20-million-yen account until you lose 600,000 yen in a day or 1.2 million yen in total, and if you follow the rules properly you can withdraw the profits. That's roughly how it is. Account sizes go up to 35 million yen. If you have little money and keep melting small accounts with leverage, you should consider prop. If you're going all-in with all the savings you built up from part-time work, look into prop! In this world, using leverage like Kurumi-chan to turn 300,000 yen into 20 million isn't impossible, but well, the difficulty is high. #FXWarriorKurumi
